item.title: Dart Programming Examples: 30 Simple Programs with Output
item.description:
These are the small programs every beginner writes, solved in clear, modern Dart. Each one shows the code and the output. Press Run to try it in the browser, then change it: use other numbers, add a feature, break it on purpose and read the error. That is the fastest way to learn Dart.

The examples go from very easy to intermediate. If a keyword is new to you, follow the link under the example to the lesson that explains it.

item.title: Classes and Objects in Dart
item.description:
A class is a blueprint. An object is a thing built from that blueprint. The class Car describes what every car has and can do; your car and your neighbour’s car are two objects of that class.

Defining a class

class Dog {
 // Fields: the data each dog has.
 String name;
 int age;

 // Constructor: runs when a dog is created.
 Dog(this.name, this.age);

 // Method: something a dog can do.
 void bark() {
 print('$name says Woof!');
 }
}

void main() {
 var dog = Dog('Bruno', 3);
 dog.bark();
 print(dog.age);
}

Bruno says Woof!
3

Class names use UpperCamelCase. Fields and methods use lowerCamelCase.

item.title: Exception Handling in Dart: try, catch, on and finally
item.description:
An exception is Dart’s way of signalling that something went wrong while the program was running. If nobody handles it, the program stops.

An unhandled exception

void main() {
 var number = int.parse('twelve');
 print(number); // never reached
}

Unhandled exception:
FormatException: Invalid radix-10 number (at character 1)
twelve
^

try and catch

Put the risky code in a try block. If it throws, control jumps to catch and the program carries on.

void main() {
 try {
 var number = int.parse('twelve');
 print(number);
 } catch (e) {
 print('That was not a number.');
 }
 print('Program continues.');
}

That was not a number.
Program continues.

Catching specific types with on

A bare catch catches everything, which can hide real bugs. Use on to handle only the problems you expect.

item.title: Formatting and Linting Dart Code: dart format and dart analyze
item.description:
Two tools keep a Dart codebase healthy without any effort from you. The formatter decides how code looks. The analyzer finds mistakes and questionable code before you run it.

dart format

The formatter rewrites your files in the standard Dart style: indentation, spacing, line breaks.

dart format . # format everything in the project
dart format lib/main.dart # one file
dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed . # check only, for CI

Before:

void main(){var names=['Asha','Bimal'];for(final n in names){print('Hello, $n');}}

After:

item.title: Functions in Dart: Defining, Calling and Returning Values
item.description:
You have been using functions since the first lesson: main is one, and so is print. Now you will write your own.

Defining and calling a function

void greet() {
 print('Hello!');
}

void main() {
 greet();
 greet();
}

Hello!
Hello!

The definition says what the function does. Nothing happens until you call it by writing its name followed by brackets.

Parameters: giving a function input

void greet(String name) {
 print('Hello, $name!');
}

void main() {
 greet('Anita');
 greet('Bishal');
}

Hello, Anita!
Hello, Bishal!

name is a parameter: a variable that exists only inside the function. The values 'Anita' and 'Bishal' are arguments.

item.title: if, else if and else in Dart
item.description:
An if statement runs a block of code only when a condition is true.

if

void main() {
 var temperature = 31;

 if (temperature > 30) {
 print('It is hot today.');
 }
}

It is hot today.

if and else

else runs when the condition is false. Exactly one of the two blocks runs.

void main() {
 var marks = 38;

 if (marks >= 40) {
 print('Pass');
 } else {
 print('Fail');
 }
}

Fail

else if

Chain as many checks as you need. Dart tests them from the top and runs the first one that is true, then skips the rest.

item.title: Imports in Dart: import, as, show and hide
item.description:
In Dart, every .dart file is a library. To use something defined in another library, you import it.

Three kinds of import

// 1. A library built into the Dart SDK
import 'dart:math';

// 2. A library from a package (your own project or one from pub.dev)
import 'package:http/http.dart';

// 3. A file in your project, by relative path
import 'utils/formatters.dart';

Imports go at the top of the file, before any other code.

item.title: Asynchronous Programming in Dart: An Introduction
item.description:
Synchronous code: one thing at a time

Normal code is synchronous. Each line finishes before the next starts.

void main() {
 print('Order coffee');
 print('Make coffee');
 print('Drink coffee');
}

That is fine when every step is instant. Now imagine a step that takes three seconds, such as downloading a photo. If the program simply waited, nothing else could happen. In an app, the screen would freeze: no scrolling, no animations, no response to taps.

item.title: Working with JSON in Dart: Encode, Decode and Model Classes
item.description:
JSON is the format most web APIs use to exchange data. It is plain text made of objects ({}), arrays ([]), strings, numbers, booleans and null. Dart’s dart:convert library translates between JSON text and Dart values.

JSON Dart
object { } Map<String, dynamic>
array [ ] List<dynamic>
string String
number int or double
true / false bool
null null

Decoding: JSON text to Dart

import 'dart:convert';

void main() {
 const text = '{"name": "Asha", "age": 28, "skills": ["Dart", "Flutter"]}';

 final data = jsonDecode(text) as Map<String, dynamic>;

 print(data['name']);
 print(data['age'] + 1);
 print(data['skills'][0]);
 print(data['email']); // missing key
}

Asha
29
Dart
null

jsonDecode returns dynamic, because the shape of the data is only known when the program runs. Working with raw maps is error-prone: a typo in a key gives null, not an error.

item.title: Null Safety in Dart: Nullable and Non-Nullable Types
item.description:
null means “no value”. It is useful: a user may have no middle name, a search may find nothing. The danger comes from forgetting that a value might be missing and using it anyway.

Dart’s answer is sound null safety: every type is non-nullable unless you say otherwise, and the compiler checks every use.

Non-nullable by default

void main() {
 String name = 'Dart';
 // name = null; // error: null can't be assigned to String

 print(name.length); // always safe
}

4

Because name can never be null, name.length can never crash.

item.title: Dart Collections: List, Set and Map Overview
item.description:
Dart has three core collection types. Picking the right one makes your code shorter and faster.

Type Ordered? Duplicates? Find items by Literal
List Yes Allowed Position (index) [1, 2, 3]
Set Insertion order Not allowed The value itself {1, 2, 3}
Map Insertion order Keys are unique Key {'a': 1}

All three at a glance

void main() {
 // List: an ordered sequence.
 var queue = ['Asha', 'Bimal', 'Asha'];

 // Set: unique values.
 var visitors = {'Asha', 'Bimal', 'Asha'};

 // Map: look up a value by its key.
 var ages = {'Asha': 24, 'Bimal': 31};

 print(queue);
 print(visitors);
 print(ages['Bimal']);
}

[Asha, Bimal, Asha]
{Asha, Bimal}
31

Collection literals

A literal is a collection written directly in code. Square brackets make a list. Curly braces make a set, or a map when the items are key: value pairs.

item.title: Reading Files in Dart
item.description:
To work with a file, create a File object from its path. This does not open or create anything. It is only a reference to a location on disk.

For the examples, assume a file notes.txt with this content:

Buy milk
Call Hari
Finish the Dart tutorial

Read the whole file as a string

import 'dart:io';

Future<void> main() async {
 final file = File('notes.txt');

 final contents = await file.readAsString();
 print(contents);
 print('${contents.length} characters');
}

Buy milk
Call Hari
Finish the Dart tutorial

44 characters

readAsString returns a Future<String>, so it must be awaited. Text is decoded as UTF-8 unless you pass another encoding.

item.title: Records in Dart: Return Multiple Values Without a Class
item.description:
A record is a small, fixed-size bundle of values. It is the quickest way to group a few things together, and the standard way to return more than one value from a function without writing a class.

Creating a record

Write the values in round brackets, separated by commas.

void main() {
 var person = ('Asha', 28);

 print(person);
 print(person.$1); // first field
 print(person.$2); // second field
}

(Asha, 28)
Asha
28

Positional fields are read with $1, $2, $3 and so on. Counting starts at 1.

item.title: Variables in Dart: var, Explicit Types and dynamic
item.description:
A variable is a name that refers to a value. You create one, give it a value, and use the name wherever you need that value.

Declaring a variable with var

void main() {
 var city = 'Kathmandu';
 var population = 1442000;
 var isCapital = true;

 print('$city, population $population, capital: $isCapital');
}

Kathmandu, population 1442000, capital: true

var tells Dart to work out the type from the value. city is a String, population is an int and isCapital is a bool. This is called type inference.

item.title: What Is Dart? An Introduction to the Dart Language
item.description:
Dart is a programming language created by Google. It was first shown in 2011, and today it is best known as the language behind Flutter, the toolkit used to build apps for Android, iOS, web, Windows, macOS and Linux from one codebase.

You can also use Dart on its own for command-line tools, servers and scripts. This tutorial teaches the language itself, so everything you learn here applies whether or not you go on to Flutter.

item.title: Constructors in Dart: Default, Named, Initializer Lists and Redirecting
item.description:
A constructor creates an object and makes sure its fields have values. Dart offers several styles, and the short ones cover most needs.

The default constructor

If you write no constructor, Dart gives you one with no parameters. Fields then need default values.

class Light {
 bool isOn = false;
 int brightness = 50;
}

void main() {
 var light = Light();
 print('${light.isOn} ${light.brightness}');
}

false 50

Initializing formals

Writing this.name in the parameter list assigns the argument straight to the field. This is the form you will write most.

item.title: Creating Your Own Libraries in Dart
item.description:
As a project grows, one file becomes hundreds of lines and then thousands. Splitting code into libraries keeps each piece small, lets you hide implementation details, and makes the code reusable.

A file is a library

You already know how to make a library: create a .dart file.

// File: lib/temperature.dart

double celsiusToFahrenheit(double c) => c * 9 / 5 + 32;

double fahrenheitToCelsius(double f) => (f - 32) * 5 / 9;

// Private: only usable inside this file.
double _round(double value) => (value * 10).round() / 10;

String describe(double celsius) =>
 '${_round(celsius)}°C is ${_round(celsiusToFahrenheit(celsius))}°F';

// File: bin/main.dart
import 'package:my_app/temperature.dart';

void main() {
 print(describe(36.6));
 // _round(1.23); // error: private to temperature.dart
}

36.6°C is 97.9°F

Names starting with _ are invisible outside the file. This is how a library separates its public API from its internals.

item.title: Custom Exceptions in Dart
item.description:
The built-in exception types are general. Your app has its own failures: “insufficient balance”, “user not found”, “session expired”. A custom exception gives each of them a name, so callers can handle them precisely and carry useful data along.

A minimal custom exception

Implement the Exception interface. It has no required members.

class InsufficientFundsException implements Exception {
 final double balance;
 final double requested;

 InsufficientFundsException(this.balance, this.requested);

 @override
 String toString() =>
 'InsufficientFundsException: tried to withdraw $requested, '
 'but the balance is $balance';
}

class Account {
 double balance;
 Account(this.balance);

 void withdraw(double amount) {
 if (amount > balance) {
 throw InsufficientFundsException(balance, amount);
 }
 balance -= amount;
 }
}

void main() {
 var account = Account(500);

 try {
 account.withdraw(200);
 account.withdraw(800);
 } on InsufficientFundsException catch (e) {
 print(e);
 print('You are short by ${e.requested - e.balance}');
 }
}

InsufficientFundsException: tried to withdraw 800.0, but the balance is 300.0
You are short by 500.0

Because the exception carries balance and requested, the handler can do something specific with them.

item.title: Data Types in Dart: A Complete Overview
item.description:
Every value in Dart has a type, and the type decides what you can do with the value. You can add two numbers, but you cannot add a number to a true.

The built-in types

Type Holds Example
int Whole numbers 42, -7
double Numbers with a decimal point 3.14, -0.5
num Either an int or a double 42, 3.14
String Text 'hello'
bool True or false true, false
List An ordered group of values [1, 2, 3]
Set A group of unique values {1, 2, 3}
Map Key and value pairs {'a': 1}
Record A fixed bundle of values ('Ana', 30)
Null The single value null null

Seeing the types in action

void main() {
 int apples = 12;
 double price = 4.5;
 String fruit = 'apple';
 bool inStock = true;
 List<String> colours = ['red', 'green'];
 Set<int> sizes = {1, 2, 3};
 Map<String, double> prices = {'apple': 4.5, 'pear': 6.0};
 (String, int) pair = ('apple', 12);

 print(apples.runtimeType);
 print(price.runtimeType);
 print(fruit.runtimeType);
 print(inStock.runtimeType);
 print(colours.runtimeType);
 print(pair.runtimeType);
 print('$sizes $prices');
}

int
double
String
bool
List<String>
(String, int)
{1, 2, 3} {apple: 4.5, pear: 6.0}

runtimeType tells you the type of a value while the program runs. It is handy for learning and debugging.

item.title: Debugging Dart Code: Breakpoints and Dart DevTools
item.description:
Sprinkling print statements around works for small problems. For anything more, a debugger is faster: it pauses your program at a line you choose and lets you look at every variable.

A program with a bug

double average(List<int> marks) {
 var total = 0;
 for (var i = 0; i <= marks.length; i++) { // bug: should be <
 total += marks[i];
 }
 return total / marks.length;
}

void main() {
 print(average([70, 85, 90]));
}

Running this throws a RangeError. Let us find out why without guessing.

Breakpoints

A breakpoint marks a line where the program should pause.

item.title: Future in Dart: Working with Values That Arrive Later
item.description:
A Future<T> is an object that represents a value of type T that will be available at some point. It is the return type of nearly every asynchronous function in Dart.

The three states

A future is always in one of these states:

  1. Uncompleted: the work is still going on.
  2. Completed with a value: it succeeded and holds the result.
  3. Completed with an error: it failed and holds an exception.

Once completed, a future never changes again.

item.title: HTTP Requests in Dart: GET, POST and Calling REST APIs
item.description:
Most apps talk to a server: to log in, load a feed, or save an order. In Dart the standard tool is the http package.

dart pub add http

The examples use JSONPlaceholder, a free practice API.

A GET request

import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;

Future<void> main() async {
 final url = Uri.parse('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1');

 final response = await http.get(url);

 print(response.statusCode);
 print(response.headers['content-type']);
 print(response.body);
}

200
application/json; charset=utf-8
{
 "userId": 1,
 "id": 1,
 "title": "sunt aut facere repellat provident occaecati excepturi optio reprehenderit",
 "body": "quia et suscipit..."
}

http.get returns a Future<Response>. The body is a string; decode it to use the data.

item.description:
You can start learning in the browser with DartPad, but sooner or later you will want Dart on your own machine. That means installing the Dart SDK, which contains the dart command, the compilers and the core libraries.

If you already installed Flutter, you have Dart. Flutter ships with its own copy of the SDK. Run dart --version to confirm.

Windows

The easiest route is the Chocolatey package manager. Open PowerShell as administrator and run:

item.title: Lists in Dart: Create, Access, Add, Remove and Sort
item.description:
A List is an ordered collection, the same idea other languages call an array. Each item has a position, called its index, starting at 0.

Creating and reading

void main() {
 var fruits = ['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'];

 print(fruits[0]);
 print(fruits[fruits.length - 1]);
 print(fruits.first);
 print(fruits.last);
 print(fruits.length);
}

apple
cherry
apple
cherry
3

Asking for an index that does not exist, such as fruits[5], throws a RangeError.

Changing items

void main() {
 var fruits = ['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'];

 fruits[1] = 'blueberry'; // replace
 fruits.add('date'); // add to the end
 fruits.addAll(['fig', 'grape']); // add several
 fruits.insert(0, 'apricot'); // add at a position

 print(fruits);
}

[apricot, apple, blueberry, cherry, date, fig, grape]

Removing items

void main() {
 var numbers = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60];

 numbers.remove(30); // by value
 numbers.removeAt(0); // by index
 numbers.removeLast();
 numbers.removeWhere((n) => n > 45); // by condition

 print(numbers);
 numbers.clear();
 print(numbers);
}

[20, 40]
[]

Searching

void main() {
 var names = ['Ram', 'Sita', 'Hari', 'Gita'];

 print(names.contains('Hari'));
 print(names.indexOf('Hari'));
 print(names.indexOf('Nobody')); // -1 means not found
 print(names.firstWhere((n) => n.endsWith('ita')));
 print(names.indexWhere((n) => n.startsWith('G')));
}

true
2
-1
Sita
3

Sorting and reversing

sort changes the list itself. reversed gives back a new view and leaves the list alone.

item.title: Null-Aware Operators in Dart: ?., ??, ??= and !
item.description:
Checking for null with if works, but it gets wordy. Dart has a set of small operators that handle the common cases in a few characters.

?? gives a default

a ?? b means “use a, but if it is null use b”.

void main() {
 String? nickname;
 var display = nickname ?? 'Guest';
 print(display);

 nickname = 'Sunny';
 print(nickname ?? 'Guest');
}

Guest
Sunny

The result of ?? is non-nullable when the right-hand side is, so display is a plain String.

item.title: Function Parameters in Dart: Positional, Named, Optional and Default
item.description:
Dart gives you several ways to pass values into a function. Choosing well makes your functions easier to call correctly.

Required positional parameters

The plain kind. Arguments are matched by position, and every one must be supplied.

String fullName(String first, String last) {
 return '$first $last';
}

void main() {
 print(fullName('Ada', 'Lovelace'));
}

Ada Lovelace

Optional positional parameters

Wrap parameters in [ ] to make them optional. Without a default they are null when left out, so their type needs a ?.

item.title: Patterns and Destructuring in Dart
item.description:
A pattern describes the shape of a value. Dart can use it to do two things at once:

  • Match: check whether a value has that shape.
  • Destructure: pull the pieces out into variables.

Patterns appear in variable declarations, assignments, for loops, if, and switch.

Destructuring in a declaration

void main() {
 var [first, second, third] = [10, 20, 30];
 print(first + second + third);

 var (name, age) = ('Asha', 28);
 print('$name is $age');

 var {'host': host, 'port': port} = {'host': 'localhost', 'port': 8080};
 print('$host:$port');
}

60
Asha is 28
localhost:8080

In a declaration the pattern must be certain to match. var [a, b] = [1, 2, 3]; throws, because the lengths differ.

item.title: Dart Practice Projects and Exercises for Beginners
item.description:
Reading about Dart gives you knowledge. Building things gives you skill. This page lists projects in rising order of difficulty. All of them can be written as command-line programs with plain Dart, with no Flutter needed.

How to get the most from a project

  1. Build the smallest version first. One feature, working end to end.
  2. Type the code yourself. Do not copy and paste.
  3. Get stuck on purpose. Struggle for twenty minutes before searching. That is when the learning happens.
  4. Refactor when it works. Rename things, split big functions, remove repetition.
  5. Add tests to at least one project.
  6. Put it on GitHub, with a README. A few finished projects are worth more than many unfinished ones.

Beginner projects

These use the first five chapters: basics, control flow, functions and collections.

item.title: The Ternary Operator in Dart (condition ? a : b)
item.description:
The ternary operator is a compact if/else that produces a value.

condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse

Basic use

void main() {
 var age = 17;
 var status = age >= 18 ? 'adult' : 'minor';
 print(status);
}

minor

The same thing with if takes five lines and needs the variable declared first:

void main() {
 var age = 17;
 String status;
 if (age >= 18) {
 status = 'adult';
 } else {
 status = 'minor';
 }
 print(status);
}

Inside other expressions

Because it is an expression, a ternary can sit anywhere a value can.

void main() {
 var items = 1;
 print('You have $items ${items == 1 ? 'item' : 'items'} in your cart.');

 var stock = 0;
 print(stock > 0 ? 'In stock' : 'Sold out');
}

You have 1 item in your cart.
Sold out

Chaining

You can chain ternaries to pick between more than two values. Lay each branch on its own line so it reads like a table.

item.title: Writing Files in Dart
item.description:
Writing is as direct as reading. One method call creates the file if needed and puts your text in it.

Write a string

import 'dart:io';

Future<void> main() async {
 final file = File('greeting.txt');

 await file.writeAsString('Hello, file!\n');
 print(await file.readAsString());
}

Hello, file!

If the file does not exist it is created. If it does exist, its contents are replaced.

Append instead of overwrite

Pass mode: FileMode.append to add to the end.

import 'dart:io';

Future<void> main() async {
 final log = File('app.log');

 await log.writeAsString('App started\n');
 await log.writeAsString('User logged in\n', mode: FileMode.append);
 await log.writeAsString('User logged out\n', mode: FileMode.append);

 print(await log.readAsString());
}

App started
User logged in
User logged out
Mode Effect
FileMode.write (default) Replace everything
FileMode.append Add to the end
FileMode.writeOnly Replace, without read access
FileMode.writeOnlyAppend Append, without read access

Write several lines

Join the lines with a newline, or build the text with a StringBuffer.

item.title: Dart List Methods: Complete Guide with Easy Examples
item.description:
The Lists lesson introduced the List type. This page collects the list methods you will reach for every day, grouped by what you want to do, each with a short program and its output. Press Run on any example, change the numbers, and run it again.

Quick reference table

Method What it does Changes the list?
add(x) / addAll(xs) Add to the end Yes
insert(i, x) / insertAll(i, xs) Add at a position Yes
remove(x) / removeAt(i) / removeLast() Remove one item Yes
removeWhere(test) / retainWhere(test) Remove by condition Yes
clear() Remove everything Yes
sort() / shuffle() Reorder Yes
contains(x) / indexOf(x) Find an item No
firstWhere(test) / indexWhere(test) Find by condition No
any(test) / every(test) Check a condition No
where(test) Keep matching items No (new iterable)
map(f) Transform each item No (new iterable)
reduce(f) / fold(start, f) Combine into one value No
sublist(a, b) / take(n) / skip(n) Get part of the list No
join(sep) Make one string No
toSet() Remove duplicates No

Methods such as where, map, take and skip return a lazy Iterable. Add .toList() when you need a real list back. The Iterable lesson explains why.

item.title: Arrow Functions in Dart (=> Syntax)
item.description:
When a function body is a single expression, Dart lets you replace the braces and return with =>.

Block body and arrow body

These two functions are identical:

int doubleIt(int n) {
 return n * 2;
}

int doubleItShort(int n) => n * 2;

void main() {
 print(doubleIt(21));
 print(doubleItShort(21));
}

42
42

Read => expression as “returns this expression”.

More examples

bool isAdult(int age) => age >= 18;

String initials(String first, String last) => '${first[0]}${last[0]}';

double circleArea(double r) => 3.14159 * r * r;

void log(String message) => print('[LOG] $message');

void main() {
 print(isAdult(20));
 print(initials('Grace', 'Hopper'));
 print(circleArea(2));
 log('Started');
}

true
GH
12.56636
[LOG] Started

log returns nothing, but => is still allowed because print(...) is a single expression.

item.title: async and await in Dart
item.description:
async and await are two keywords that let you work with futures as if the code were synchronous. They do not add new abilities. They make asynchronous code readable.

The two rules

  1. Mark a function async to be allowed to use await inside it. An async function always returns a Future.
  2. Put await before a future to pause the function until that future completes, and get its value.
Future<String> fetchGreeting() async {
 await Future.delayed(Duration(seconds: 1));
 return 'Namaste'; // automatically wrapped in a Future<String>
}

Future<void> main() async {
 print('Loading...');
 final greeting = await fetchGreeting();
 print(greeting);
}

Loading...
Namaste

Inside fetchGreeting you return a plain String. Because the function is async, the caller receives a Future<String>.

item.title: Checking If a File Exists and Deleting Files in Dart
item.description:
Before reading a file you may want to know whether it is there. When you are done with one, you may want to remove it, rename it or copy it.

Does it exist?

import 'dart:io';

Future<void> main() async {
 final file = File('notes.txt');

 if (await file.exists()) {
 print('Found ${file.path}');
 } else {
 print('${file.path} is missing');
 }

 // Synchronous version
 print(File('pubspec.yaml').existsSync());
}

File.exists() is true only if the path exists and is a file. For a folder, use Directory(path).exists().

What kind of thing is at this path?

When you do not know whether a path is a file, a folder or a link, ask FileSystemEntity.

item.title: Date and Time in Dart: DateTime and Duration
item.description:
Dart handles dates with two classes. DateTime is a moment in time. Duration is a length of time.

Creating a DateTime

void main() {
 final now = DateTime.now();
 final birthday = DateTime(1998, 4, 23);
 final meeting = DateTime(2026, 10, 15, 14, 30);
 final parsed = DateTime.parse('2026-12-31T23:59:00');

 print(now.year >= 2026);
 print(birthday);
 print(meeting);
 print(parsed);
}

true
1998-04-23 00:00:00.000
2026-10-15 14:30:00.000
2026-12-31 23:59:00.000

Months are numbered 1 to 12 and days start at 1, as you would expect.

DateTime.parse throws on text it cannot read. Use DateTime.tryParse, which returns null, for input you do not control.

item.title: Factory Constructors in Dart
item.description:
A normal constructor always creates a brand-new object of its own class. A factory constructor is a constructor that gets to decide what to return. It can hand back an existing object, an object of a subclass, or a new object after doing some checks.

To the caller it looks exactly like any other constructor.

Syntax

class Temperature {
 final double celsius;
 Temperature(this.celsius);

 factory Temperature.fromFahrenheit(double f) {
 return Temperature((f - 32) * 5 / 9);
 }
}

void main() {
 var t = Temperature.fromFahrenheit(212);
 print(t.celsius);
}

100.0

A factory constructor has a body that returns an object. It cannot use this, because no object exists until it creates or finds one.

item.title: Dart Interview Questions and Answers
item.description:
These are the questions that come up most in Dart and Flutter interviews. Each answer is short on purpose, and links to the lesson that covers the topic in depth. Try to answer each one aloud before reading on.

Language basics

1. What is Dart, and where is it used?
Dart is a typed, object-oriented language from Google. It is the language of Flutter, and is also used for command-line tools, servers and web apps. See what is Dart.

item.title: The late Keyword in Dart: Late and Lazy Initialization
item.description:
Dart insists that a non-nullable variable has a value before it is used. Sometimes you know it will, but the compiler cannot see it. The late keyword says: “I will give this a value later, before I read it.”

The problem

class Thermometer {
 // double reading; // error: non-nullable field must be initialized

 late double reading;

 void measure() {
 reading = 36.6;
 }
}

void main() {
 var t = Thermometer();
 t.measure();
 print(t.reading);
}

36.6

Without late you would have to make reading nullable and then check for null everywhere it is used.

item.title: Logging in Dart: print, dart:developer and the logging Package
item.description:
A debugger shows what is happening now, on your machine. Logs record what happened earlier, including on a user’s device or a server you cannot attach to. Good logs turn “it crashed” into “it crashed after the third retry because the token had expired”.

print: fine for learning, limited for apps

void main() {
 print('Loading user 42');
}

print has no levels, no timestamps and no way to switch it off, and in a released app it still runs. Use it in scripts and while experimenting. The avoid_print lint will remind you to replace it in real projects.

item.title: Numbers in Dart: int, double and num
item.description:
Dart has two number types. int holds whole numbers and double holds numbers with a fractional part. Both are kinds of num.

Arithmetic

void main() {
 var a = 17;
 var b = 5;

 print(a + b); // addition
 print(a - b); // subtraction
 print(a * b); // multiplication
 print(a / b); // division, always a double
 print(a ~/ b); // integer division
 print(a % b); // remainder
}

22
12
85
3.4
3
2

The / operator always returns a double, even for 10 / 2, which gives 5.0. Use ~/ when you want a whole number.

item.title: switch and case in Dart
item.description:
A switch compares one value against a list of cases and runs the first one that matches. It is tidier than a long else if chain when every branch tests the same value.

A basic switch

void main() {
 var day = 3;

 switch (day) {
 case 1:
 print('Monday');
 case 2:
 print('Tuesday');
 case 3:
 print('Wednesday');
 default:
 print('Another day');
 }
}

Wednesday

Since Dart 3, a case that contains code ends on its own. You do not need break, and one case never falls into the next.

item.title: Switch Expressions in Dart 3
item.description:
A switch statement runs code. A switch expression produces a value. It is shorter, has no case or break, and can be used anywhere a value is expected.

From statement to expression

enum Level { low, medium, high }

String colourStatement(Level level) {
 switch (level) {
 case Level.low:
 return 'green';
 case Level.medium:
 return 'orange';
 case Level.high:
 return 'red';
 }
}

String colourExpression(Level level) => switch (level) {
 Level.low => 'green',
 Level.medium => 'orange',
 Level.high => 'red',
 };

void main() {
 print(colourStatement(Level.high));
 print(colourExpression(Level.medium));
}

red
orange

The syntax

var result = switch (value) {
 pattern1 => expression1,
 pattern2 => expression2,
 _ => defaultExpression,
};
  • Each case is pattern => expression, separated by commas.
  • _ is the wildcard that matches anything, like default.
  • When assigned to a variable, the whole thing ends with a semicolon.

Matching values, ranges and alternatives

String describeMark(int mark) => switch (mark) {
 100 => 'Perfect',
 >= 90 => 'Excellent',
 >= 60 && < 90 => 'Good',
 40 || 41 || 42 => 'Just passed',
 < 40 => 'Failed',
 _ => 'Passed',
 };

void main() {
 for (final m in [100, 95, 70, 41, 20, 50]) {
 print('$m: ${describeMark(m)}');
 }
}

100: Perfect
95: Excellent
70: Good
41: Just passed
20: Failed
50: Passed

Cases are tried from top to bottom, and the first match wins.

item.title: Using Packages from pub.dev in Dart
item.description:
A package is a bundle of Dart code that someone has published for others to use. pub.dev is the official home of Dart and Flutter packages, with tens of thousands available for HTTP, databases, dates, state management, testing and much more.

pubspec.yaml

Every Dart project has a pubspec.yaml at its root. It names the project and lists what it depends on.

name: my_app
description: A sample command-line application.
version: 1.0.0

environment:
 sdk: ^3.5.0

dependencies:
 http: ^1.2.0
 path: ^1.9.0

dev_dependencies:
 lints: ^5.0.0
 test: ^1.25.0
Section Meaning
environment Which Dart SDK versions the project supports
dependencies Packages the program needs to run
dev_dependencies Packages needed only while developing: tests, linters, code generators

YAML uses indentation for structure. Use two spaces, never tabs.

item.title: Your First Dart Program: Hello World Explained
item.description:
Every Dart program, from a five-line script to a full mobile app, starts running at the same place: a function called main.

Hello, world

Create a file named hello.dart and type this in:

void main() {
 print('Hello, world!');
}

Run it from the terminal with dart run hello.dart, or press Run above.

Hello, world!

Reading the program piece by piece

Part Meaning
void The function gives nothing back when it finishes
main The special name Dart looks for to start the program
() The function takes no input here
{ ... } The body: the statements that run, top to bottom
print(...) A built-in function that writes a line to the console
'Hello, world!' A string, which is a piece of text
; Ends a statement. Dart requires it

Statements run in order

void main() {
 print('Step 1: boil water');
 print('Step 2: add tea');
 print('Step 3: wait three minutes');
}

Step 1: boil water
Step 2: add tea
Step 3: wait three minutes

Printing values, not just text

print accepts any value. Put a $ in front of a variable name inside a string to drop its value in. Use ${...} for a calculation.

item.title: Anonymous Functions and Closures in Dart
item.description:
In Dart a function is a value, like a number or a string. You can store it in a variable, put it in a list or pass it to another function. A function written without a name is called an anonymous function, or lambda.

Writing an anonymous function

Take a normal function, remove the name, and you have one.

void main() {
 var numbers = [1, 2, 3];

 numbers.forEach((n) {
 print(n * 10);
 });
}

10
20
30

(n) { print(n * 10); } has parameters and a body but no name. It is created right where it is needed.

item.title: Error Handling in Asynchronous Dart Code
item.description:
Asynchronous operations fail more often than ordinary code, because they depend on networks, files and other services. The good news: with await, you handle those failures with the same try/catch you already know.

try and catch with await

Future<String> fetchWeather(String city) async {
 await Future.delayed(Duration(milliseconds: 300));
 if (city.isEmpty) throw ArgumentError('City is required');
 if (city == 'Atlantis') throw Exception('City not found');
 return '$city: 24 degrees';
}

Future<void> show(String city) async {
 try {
 print(await fetchWeather(city));
 } on ArgumentError catch (e) {
 print('Invalid input: ${e.message}');
 } catch (e) {
 print('Could not load weather: $e');
 } finally {
 print('Request for "$city" finished');
 }
}

Future<void> main() async {
 await show('Pokhara');
 await show('Atlantis');
 await show('');
}

Pokhara: 24 degrees
Request for "Pokhara" finished
Could not load weather: Exception: City not found
Request for "Atlantis" finished
Invalid input: City is required
Request for "" finished

The mistake that makes catch useless

try/catch only catches errors from futures you await inside it. Without await, the future fails later, after the try block has already ended.

item.title: Comments in Dart: Single-Line, Multi-Line and Doc Comments
item.description:
A comment is a note in your code that Dart ignores. Comments are for people: your teammates, and you in six months.

Single-line comments

Everything after // on a line is ignored.

void main() {
 // Price before tax.
 var price = 200;

 var total = price * 1.13; // 13% VAT
 print(total);
}

226.0

Multi-line comments

Text between /* and */ is ignored, across as many lines as you like. This form is mostly used to switch off a block of code for a moment.

item.title: Const Constructors in Dart: Immutable Objects
item.description:
A const constructor lets a class produce compile-time constants: objects that are created once, can never change, and are shared wherever the same values are used.

Requirements

A class can have a const constructor when every field is final.

class Point {
 final int x;
 final int y;

 const Point(this.x, this.y);
}

void main() {
 const a = Point(1, 2);
 const b = Point(1, 2);
 var c = Point(1, 2); // not const: a new object each time

 print(identical(a, b));
 print(identical(a, c));
}

true
false

a and b are the same single object in memory. Dart calls this canonicalization. c was created without const, so it is a separate object even though its values match.

item.title: Dart Cheat Sheet: Syntax Quick Reference
item.description:
A compact reference for the syntax you use most. Each section links to the full lesson.

Variables

Full lesson: Variables in Dart.

var name = 'Asha'; // type inferred, can be reassigned
String city = 'Pokhara'; // explicit type
final age = 28; // set once, at run time
const pi = 3.14159; // compile-time constant
int? score; // nullable, starts as null
late String token; // set later, before first use
dynamic anything = 42; // no static checking

Built-in types

Full lesson: Built-in types in Dart.

int count = 10;
double price = 9.99;
num either = 3; // int or double
bool isReady = true;
String text = 'hello';
List<int> list = [1, 2, 3];
Set<String> tags = {'a', 'b'};
Map<String, int> ages = {'Asha': 28};
(String, int) pair = ('x', 1); // record
({String name, int age}) person = (name: 'Bimal', age: 31);

Strings

Full lesson: Strings in Dart.

item.title: Working with Directories in Dart
item.description:
A Directory object represents a folder, in the same way a File represents a file.

Create a directory

import 'dart:io';

Future<void> main() async {
 final dir = Directory('output/reports/2026');

 await dir.create(recursive: true); // creates missing parents too
 print(await dir.exists());
}

true

Without recursive: true, the call fails unless output/reports already exists. Creating a directory that is already there is not an error.

List the contents

list() returns a stream of entries. Each one is a File, a Directory or a Link.

item.title: Loops in Dart: for, for-in, while and do-while
item.description:
A loop runs the same block of code many times. Dart has four loop statements; which you choose depends on what you know before the loop starts.

for: when you know how many times

void main() {
 for (var i = 1; i <= 5; i++) {
 print('Count: $i');
 }
}

Count: 1
Count: 2
Count: 3
Count: 4
Count: 5

The three parts in the brackets are: start (var i = 1), keep going while (i <= 5) and after each round (i++).

item.title: Memory Management and Garbage Collection in Dart
item.description:
In Dart you create objects and never delete them. Freeing memory is the job of the garbage collector (GC), which runs automatically. You do not need to manage memory by hand, but knowing how the collector works helps you write faster code and avoid leaks.

Where values live

  • The stack holds local variables and the chain of function calls. It grows and shrinks automatically as functions are called and return.
  • The heap holds objects. A variable on the stack holds a reference to an object on the heap.
class User {
 String name;
 User(this.name);
}

void main() {
 var a = User('Asha'); // object on the heap, reference in a
 var b = a; // second reference, same object
 b.name = 'Bimal';
 print(a.name);
}

Bimal

When is an object garbage?

An object can be freed once it is unreachable: nothing your program can still get to holds a reference to it.

item.title: Creating and Publishing a Dart Package
item.description:
Publishing a package is how you share reusable code with every Dart developer. It is also a good way to sharpen your skills, since publishing forces you to think about API design, documentation and testing.

1. Create the package

dart create -t package string_tools
cd string_tools

For a package containing Flutter widgets, use flutter create --template=package.

string_tools/
 lib/
 string_tools.dart # public API: exports
 src/
 string_tools_base.dart # implementation
 test/
 string_tools_test.dart
 example/
 string_tools_example.dart
 pubspec.yaml
 README.md
 CHANGELOG.md
 LICENSE
 analysis_options.yaml

2. Write the code

// File: lib/src/casing.dart

/// Extra helpers for changing the case of a [String].
extension Casing on String {
 /// Returns this string with its first letter in upper case.
 ///
 /// For example, `'dart'.capitalized` is `'Dart'`.
 String get capitalized =>
 isEmpty ? this : '${this[0].toUpperCase()}${substring(1)}';

 /// Converts `hello world` to `Hello World`.
 String get titleCase =>
 split(' ').map((word) => word.capitalized).join(' ');
}

// File: lib/string_tools.dart

/// Small, dependency-free string utilities.
library;

export 'src/casing.dart';

Every public member should have a /// doc comment. They become your API reference on pub.dev.

item.title: Regular Expressions in Dart with RegExp
item.description:
A regular expression (regex) is a pattern that describes text. With one you can check whether a string has a certain shape, pull pieces out of it, or replace parts of it. In Dart, regular expressions are RegExp objects.

Always write the pattern as a raw string, r'...', so that backslashes are not treated as escapes by Dart.

Does it match?

void main() {
 final digitsOnly = RegExp(r'^\d+$');

 print(digitsOnly.hasMatch('12345'));
 print(digitsOnly.hasMatch('123a5'));
 print(RegExp(r'cat').hasMatch('concatenate')); // found anywhere
}

true
false
true

Without ^ (start) and $ (end), a pattern matches if it is found anywhere in the text.

item.title: Sealed Classes in Dart: Exhaustive Type Hierarchies
item.description:
A sealed class is a parent class with a closed list of children. All direct subtypes must be declared in the same file, so the compiler knows every one of them. In return, a switch over the sealed type is checked: if you forget a case, the code does not compile.

Think of it as an enum where each value can carry its own different data.

Declaring a sealed hierarchy

sealed class Shape {}

class Circle extends Shape {
 final double radius;
 Circle(this.radius);
}

class Rectangle extends Shape {
 final double width, height;
 Rectangle(this.width, this.height);
}

class Triangle extends Shape {
 final double base, height;
 Triangle(this.base, this.height);
}

double area(Shape shape) => switch (shape) {
 Circle(:var radius) => 3.14159 * radius * radius,
 Rectangle(:var width, :var height) => width * height,
 Triangle(:var base, :var height) => base * height / 2,
 };

void main() {
 print(area(Circle(1)));
 print(area(Rectangle(3, 4)));
 print(area(Triangle(6, 2)));
}

3.14159
12.0
6.0

There is no default and no _. Dart knows that Circle, Rectangle and Triangle are the only possibilities. Add a Square class and area stops compiling until you handle it.

item.title: Sets in Dart: Unique Collections and Set Operations
item.description:
A Set is a collection where every value appears at most once. It is the right tool when you care about whether something is in the collection, not where or how many times.

Creating a set

void main() {
 var colours = {'red', 'green', 'blue', 'red'};
 print(colours);
 print(colours.length);

 var empty = <String>{};
 print(empty.isEmpty);
}

{red, green, blue}
3
true

The duplicate 'red' is dropped silently. Dart’s default set remembers the order in which items were added.

Adding and removing

add returns true if the value was new, and false if it was already there.

item.title: Strings in Dart: Interpolation, Methods and Multi-Line Text
item.description:
A String is a piece of text. You can write one with single or double quotes; Dart style uses single quotes unless the text itself contains one.

void main() {
 var a = 'Hello';
 var b = "It's easy";
 print('$a. $b.');
}

Hello. It's easy.

String interpolation

Put $name inside a string to insert a variable. Wrap any other expression in ${ }.

void main() {
 var item = 'coffee';
 var price = 3.5;
 var qty = 2;

 print('$qty x $item = ${price * qty}');
 print('${item.toUpperCase()} has ${item.length} letters');
}

2 x coffee = 7.0
COFFEE has 6 letters

Joining strings

void main() {
 var first = 'Dart';
 var second = 'Tutorial';

 print(first + ' ' + second); // works
 print('$first $second'); // preferred
 print('Dart ' 'Tutorial'); // neighbouring literals join automatically
}

Dart Tutorial
Dart Tutorial
Dart Tutorial

Multi-line and raw strings

Three quotes let a string run over several lines. An r before the quote makes a raw string, where \ and $ are just characters.

item.title: Common Dart Errors and How to Fix Them: A Troubleshooting Guide
item.description:
Every Dart developer sees the same errors again and again. This guide lists the most common ones, explains what each error means in plain words, and shows how to fix it. Use your browser’s search (Ctrl+F or Cmd+F) to jump to the message you are seeing.

There are two kinds of errors:

Kind When you see it Example
Compile-time error In the editor, before the program runs (red underline) The argument type 'String?' can't be assigned...
Runtime error (exception) While the program runs Null check operator used on a null value

Compile-time errors are the friendly kind: Dart stops you before anything goes wrong. Start by reading how to read an error if stack traces look confusing.

item.title: Dart Syntax: The Basic Rules of Dart in One Page
item.description:
This page is a tour of Dart syntax for beginners. Each section shows one rule in a tiny program. You do not need to remember everything now: every topic links to a full lesson later in the course. If you have programmed before, this page alone is enough to start reading Dart code.

Every program starts in main

void main() {
 print('Hello, Dart!');
}

Hello, Dart!
  • void main() is where the program begins. void means it returns nothing.
  • Code that belongs together sits inside curly braces { }.
  • Each statement ends with a semicolon ;. Forgetting it is the most common beginner error.
  • print writes a line to the console.

Comments

void main() {
 // A single-line comment
 /* A comment that can
 cover several lines */
 print('Comments are ignored when the program runs');
}

Comments are ignored when the program runs

/// starts a documentation comment. See Comments.

item.title: Dart String Methods: Complete List with Easy Examples
item.description:
The Strings lesson showed how to create text and use interpolation. This page is a reference you can come back to: the string methods you will use most, grouped by job, each with a tiny program you can run and change.

Remember one rule while you read: strings never change. Every method below returns a new string (or a value) and leaves the original alone.

Quick reference table

Method or property What it does Example Result
length Number of characters 'Dart'.length 4
toUpperCase() All capitals 'dart'.toUpperCase() DART
toLowerCase() All small letters 'DART'.toLowerCase() dart
trim() Remove spaces at both ends ' hi '.trim() hi
contains(x) Is x inside? 'Flutter'.contains('utt') true
startsWith(x) Begins with x? 'Dart'.startsWith('D') true
endsWith(x) Ends with x? 'main.dart'.endsWith('.dart') true
indexOf(x) First position of x, or -1 'banana'.indexOf('a') 1
substring(a, b) Characters from a up to b 'Flutter'.substring(0, 4) Flut
split(x) Break into a list 'a,b'.split(',') [a, b]
replaceAll(a, b) Replace every a 'a-b-c'.replaceAll('-', '+') a+b+c
padLeft(n, x) Fill on the left to width n '7'.padLeft(3, '0') 007
isEmpty Has no characters? ''.isEmpty true
* Repeat 'ab' * 3 ababab

Changing case and removing spaces

void main() {
 var name = ' Dart Tutorial ';

 print('[${name.trim()}]');
 print('[${name.trimLeft()}]');
 print('[${name.trimRight()}]');
 print(name.trim().toUpperCase());
 print(name.trim().toLowerCase());
}

[Dart Tutorial]
[Dart Tutorial ]
[ Dart Tutorial]
DART TUTORIAL
dart tutorial

The square brackets are only there so you can see where the spaces are. trim() is the first thing to call on anything a user types.

item.title: break and continue in Dart
item.description:
Sometimes you need to change the flow of a loop from the inside. break stops the loop completely. continue skips the rest of the current round and moves on to the next.

break

void main() {
 var numbers = [4, 9, 15, 22, 8];

 for (final n in numbers) {
 if (n > 10) {
 print('First number over 10 is $n');
 break;
 }
 print('Checked $n');
 }
}

Checked 4
Checked 9
First number over 10 is 15

Once the answer is found there is no reason to look at 22 and 8, so break saves the work.

item.title: Building Command-Line Apps in Dart
item.description:
Dart is an excellent language for command-line tools. It starts quickly, runs on Windows, macOS and Linux, and compiles to a single file that runs without Dart installed.

Create the project

dart create -t cli word_count
cd word_count
dart run

The entry point is bin/word_count.dart.

Arguments

Whatever follows the program name arrives in main as a list of strings.

void main(List<String> arguments) {
 if (arguments.isEmpty) {
 print('Usage: greet <name>');
 return;
 }
 print('Hello, ${arguments.join(' ')}!');
}

dart run bin/greet.dart Asha Rai

Hello, Asha Rai!

Standard output, standard error and exit codes

A well-behaved tool follows three conventions.

item.title: const and Performance in Dart: Compile-Time Constants
item.description:
You have met const already as a way to say “this value is fixed”. It is also a performance tool. A constant is built once by the compiler, stored in the program itself, and never allocated or garbage collected while the app runs.

What makes something a compile-time constant

The compiler must be able to work out the complete value before the program starts.

const maxRetries = 3; // a literal
const timeout = Duration(seconds: 30); // a const constructor
const sizes = [8, 16, 24]; // a const collection
const greeting = 'Hello ' 'world'; // joined literals
const area = 12 * 12; // arithmetic on constants
const isBig = area > 100; // comparisons on constants
const label = isBig ? 'big' : 'small'; // conditional on constants

void main() {
 print('$maxRetries ${timeout.inSeconds} $sizes $greeting $area $label');
}

3 30 [8, 16, 24] Hello world 144 big

Not allowed in a constant: anything only known at run time, such as DateTime.now(), user input, the result of a normal function call, or a non-const variable.

item.title: File Paths in Dart with the path Package
item.description:
A path is a string that says where a file lives. Handling paths with plain string operations is a classic source of bugs, because Windows uses \ and everything else uses /. The official path package handles this for you.

Install it

dart pub add path

It is conventionally imported with the prefix p.

Join parts into a path

Never glue paths together with + or string interpolation. p.join inserts the right separator for the current platform.

item.title: Getters and Setters in Dart
item.description:
Getters and setters are methods that look like fields. A getter runs when you read a property, and a setter runs when you assign to it. They let a class control its data without changing how other code uses it.

Every field already has them

When you declare a field, Dart creates an invisible getter, and a setter too unless the field is final. That is why you rarely need to write trivial ones.

item.title: Higher-Order Functions in Dart
item.description:
A higher-order function is a function that takes another function as an argument, returns one, or both. They let you separate what to do from when or how often to do it.

Taking a function as a parameter

void repeat(int times, void Function(int) action) {
 for (var i = 1; i <= times; i++) {
 action(i);
 }
}

void main() {
 repeat(3, (i) => print('Round $i'));
}

Round 1
Round 2
Round 3

repeat knows how to loop. The caller decides what happens in each round.

One function, many behaviours

int calculate(int a, int b, int Function(int, int) operation) {
 return operation(a, b);
}

int add(int a, int b) => a + b;

void main() {
 print(calculate(8, 2, add));
 print(calculate(8, 2, (a, b) => a * b));
 print(calculate(8, 2, (a, b) => a ~/ b));
}

10
16
4

The built-in ones you will use daily

Dart’s collections come with higher-order functions that replace most hand-written loops.

item.title: Maps in Dart: Key-Value Pairs Explained
item.description:
A Map links keys to values. Give it a key and it returns the value, the way a dictionary gives you a definition for a word. Other languages call this a dictionary, hash map or object.

Creating and reading

void main() {
 var capitals = {
 'Nepal': 'Kathmandu',
 'Japan': 'Tokyo',
 'Kenya': 'Nairobi',
 };

 print(capitals['Japan']);
 print(capitals['Brazil']); // key not present
 print(capitals.length);
}

Tokyo
null
3

Looking up a missing key returns null rather than failing. That is why the result of map[key] is always a nullable type.

item.title: Streams in Dart: Handling a Sequence of Async Events
item.description:
A Future delivers one value later. A Stream delivers many values over time: zero, five, or an endless flow. If a future is a parcel on its way to you, a stream is a conveyor belt.

Streams are everywhere: keystrokes, WebSocket messages, download progress, sensor readings, database changes, and the chunks of a large file.

Reading a stream with await for

await for is a loop that waits for each event. It ends when the stream closes.

item.title: Dart Glossary: Programming Terms Explained in Simple Words
item.description:
New words are the hardest part of learning to program. This glossary explains the terms you will meet in Dart and Flutter in one or two simple sentences each, with a link to the lesson that teaches it properly.

A to E

Abstract class
A class you cannot create directly. It describes what subclasses must have. Abstract classes
Analyzer
The tool that checks your code for errors while you type. Run it yourself with dart analyze. Formatting and linting
Anonymous function
A function without a name, often passed to another function: (x) => x * 2. Anonymous functions and closures
AOT (ahead-of-time) compilation
Turning Dart into machine code before the program runs. Used for fast release apps and dart compile exe. What is Dart?
Argument / parameter
A parameter is the name in the function definition (int a). An argument is the value you pass (add(2, 3)). Function parameters
async / await
Keywords for waiting for slow work (network, files) without freezing the program. async and await
Class
A blueprint for objects: it groups data (fields) and behaviour (methods). Classes and objects
Closure
A function that remembers the variables around it, even after that code has finished. Closures
Collection
A value that holds many values: List, Set, Map, Queue. Collections overview
Compile-time constant (const)
A value fixed when the program is compiled, such as const pi = 3.14. final and const
Constructor
The special function that creates an object: Person('Asha', 21). Constructors
dynamic
A type that turns off type checking. Avoid it unless you really need it. Data types
Enum
A fixed set of named values, such as enum Size { small, medium, large }. Enums
Event loop
The engine that runs your async code one task at a time. Event loop
Exception
An error that happens while the program runs. Catch it with try / catch. Exceptions
Extension method
Adds a new method to an existing type, even one you did not write, such as String. Extension methods

F to L

Factory constructor
A constructor that can return an existing object or a subclass instead of always making a new one. Factory constructors
final
A variable that can be set only once. final and const
Future
A value that will be ready later, like the result of a download. Futures
Generics
Type placeholders such as List<T> that let one class or function work safely with many types. Generics
Getter / setter
Methods that look like fields: circle.area instead of circle.area(). Getters and setters
Higher-order function
A function that takes or returns another function, such as map and where. Higher-order functions
Hot reload
Updating a running app with your code changes in under a second, without losing its state. Mostly used in Flutter. Hot reload
Immutable
A value that cannot change after it is created. Immutability and copyWith
Inheritance
A class taking the fields and methods of another class with extends. Inheritance
Interface
A list of methods a class promises to have, used with implements. Interfaces
Isolate
Dart’s way to run code in parallel, each with its own memory. Isolates
Iterable
Anything you can loop over with for-in. List and Set are iterables. Iterables
JIT (just-in-time) compilation
Compiling code while it runs. Used during development, and what makes hot reload possible.
JSON
A text format for data, used by almost every web API. JSON in Dart
late
Says “this non-nullable variable will be set before it is used”. late variables
Library
A Dart file (or group of files) that you can import. Creating libraries

M to R

Map
A collection of key-value pairs, like a dictionary: {'apple': 3}. Maps
Method
A function that belongs to a class. Classes and objects
Mixin
A bundle of methods you can add to many classes with with. Mixins
Null safety
Dart’s guarantee that a variable cannot be null unless its type ends in ?. Null safety
Object
One thing made from a class. Also the type that every non-null value belongs to. Classes and objects
Package
Shared code you add from pub.dev with dart pub add. Pub packages
Pattern
A shape that a value can be matched against and taken apart, used in switch and destructuring. Patterns
Polymorphism
One piece of code working with objects of different classes through a shared type. Polymorphism
pubspec.yaml
The file that names your project and lists its packages. Pub packages
Record
A small group of values without a class: (name: 'Asha', age: 21). Records
Recursion
A function that calls itself to solve a smaller version of the problem. Recursion

S to Z

Scope
The part of the code where a variable exists, usually the nearest { }. Functions
Sealed class
A class whose subclasses are all known, so switch can check that you handled every case. Sealed classes
Set
A collection with no duplicates. Sets
Sound type system
Dart guarantees that a variable always holds a value of its declared type.
Spread operator (...)
Puts the items of one collection inside another: [...a, ...b]. Spread and collection if
Static member
A field or method that belongs to the class itself, not to each object. Static members
Stream
A sequence of values that arrive over time, like clicks or chat messages. Streams
String interpolation
Putting values inside text with $name or ${a + b}. Strings
Type inference
Dart working out a type for you: var n = 3; makes n an int. Variables
Typedef
A short name for a type, often a function type. Typedef
Widget
In Flutter, a piece of the user interface, such as Text or Button. Flutter widgets

Missing a word? Tell us on the contact page and we will add it. For quick syntax, keep the Dart cheat sheet open.

item.title: Dart vs JavaScript: Key Differences Explained with Code
item.description:
If you know JavaScript, Dart will feel familiar within an hour. The syntax looks alike, both have async and await, and both run in the browser. The big difference is that Dart checks types before your program runs, which catches many bugs early. This page shows the same ideas in both languages so you can map what you already know.

At a glance

Dart JavaScript
Types Static and sound, with type inference Dynamic (TypeScript adds static types)
Null Sound null safety: String can never be null Any value can be null or undefined
Runs on Native machine code, the Dart VM, JavaScript and WebAssembly Browsers, Node.js, Deno, Bun
Main use Flutter apps for mobile, web and desktop; CLI and server Websites, web apps, Node.js servers
Equality == (no type coercion) === recommended, == converts types
Integer division ~/ operator Math.floor(a / b)
Classes Classes, mixins, interfaces, sealed classes Classes and prototypes
Package manager pub (pub.dev) npm

Variables

// JavaScript
let count = 1;
const name = 'Asha';
count = 'one'; // allowed: the type changes

void main() {
 var count = 1; // count is an int from now on
 final name = 'Asha';
 // count = 'one'; // compile error: a String is not an int
 count = 2;
 print('$name $count');
}

Asha 2

final in Dart is like const in JavaScript: it cannot be reassigned. Dart’s const is stricter: the value must be known when the program is compiled. See final vs const.

item.title: assert in Dart: Catching Mistakes During Development
item.description:
An assert states something that must be true at that point in the program. If it is false, Dart stops with an error that points to the exact line. Asserts are a way of writing down your assumptions so the computer can check them.

Syntax

void main() {
 var age = 25;
 assert(age >= 0, 'Age cannot be negative');
 print('Age is $age');
}

The second argument is an optional message shown when the check fails.

Asserts only run in development

This is the important part. Asserts are ignored in production, so they cost nothing in a released app.

item.title: Benchmarking and Profiling Dart Code
item.description:
Developers are notoriously bad at guessing which part of a program is slow. The rule of performance work is: measure first, change second, measure again.

Stopwatch: the quick measurement

void main() {
 final watch = Stopwatch()..start();

 var sum = 0;
 for (var i = 0; i < 50000000; i++) {
 sum += i % 3;
 }

 watch.stop();
 print('Result $sum in ${watch.elapsedMilliseconds} ms');
}

Stopwatch uses a high-resolution clock that never jumps. Do not time code with DateTime.now().

Why a single measurement lies

Three things distort a naive measurement:

  1. Warm-up. With dart run, code starts in a slower mode and is optimised by the JIT compiler once it becomes “hot”. The first runs are much slower than later ones.
  2. Noise. Other programs, the garbage collector and the CPU’s power management all add variation.
  3. The wrong build. Debug builds are far slower than release builds and behave differently.

So warm up first, run many times, and look at the typical result.

item.title: Booleans in Dart: true, false and Logical Operators
item.description:
A bool has only two possible values: true and false. Booleans are how a program makes decisions.

Where booleans come from

Most booleans are the result of a comparison.

void main() {
 var age = 20;

 bool isAdult = age >= 18;
 bool isTeen = age >= 13 && age <= 19;

 print(isAdult);
 print(isTeen);
}

true
false

Combining conditions

Operator Name True when
&& and both sides are true
|| or at least one side is true
! not the value is false 
void main() {
 var hasTicket = true;
 var hasId = false;
 var isVip = true;

 print(hasTicket && hasId);
 print(hasTicket || hasId);
 print(!hasId);
 print((hasTicket && hasId) || isVip);
}

false
true
true
true

Short-circuit evaluation

Dart stops as soon as it knows the answer. With &&, if the left side is false the right side never runs. With ||, if the left side is true the right side never runs. This lets you guard a risky check.

item.title: File Attributes and Metadata in Dart
item.description:
Besides its contents, every file carries information about itself: how big it is, when it was last changed, and who may read it. This is the file’s metadata.

Size

import 'dart:io';

String readableSize(int bytes) {
 const units = ['B', 'KB', 'MB', 'GB'];
 var size = bytes.toDouble();
 var unit = 0;
 while (size >= 1024 && unit < units.length - 1) {
 size /= 1024;
 unit++;
 }
 return '${size.toStringAsFixed(unit == 0 ? 0 : 1)} ${units[unit]}';
}

Future<void> main() async {
 final file = File('pubspec.yaml');
 final bytes = await file.length();

 print('$bytes bytes');
 print(readableSize(bytes));
 print(readableSize(5368709));
}

312 bytes
312 B
5.1 MB

Last modified

import 'dart:io';

Future<void> main() async {
 final file = File('pubspec.yaml');
 final modified = await file.lastModified();
 final age = DateTime.now().difference(modified);

 print('Last modified: $modified');
 print('That was ${age.inDays} day(s) ago');
}

You can also change it with await file.setLastModified(DateTime.now()).

item.title: MapEntry in Dart: Working with Map Entries
item.description:
A map is a collection of entries. Each entry is a MapEntry object holding one key and one value. Working with entries lets you use all the list-style tools (where, map, sort) on a map.

Getting the entries

void main() {
 var scores = {'Anu': 82, 'Bikash': 67, 'Chhiring': 94};

 for (final entry in scores.entries) {
 print('${entry.key} scored ${entry.value}');
 }
}

Anu scored 82
Bikash scored 67
Chhiring scored 94

Creating an entry and building a map from entries

void main() {
 var entry = MapEntry('Dawa', 75);
 print('${entry.key}: ${entry.value}');

 var map = Map.fromEntries([
 MapEntry('x', 1),
 MapEntry('y', 2),
 ]);
 print(map);

 map.addEntries([MapEntry('z', 3)]);
 print(map);
}

Dawa: 75
{x: 1, y: 2}
{x: 1, y: 2, z: 3}

Filtering a map

Filter the entries, then turn them back into a map.

item.title: Private Members and Encapsulation in Dart
item.description:
If you come from Java or C#, you will look for public, private and protected. Dart has none of them. It has one rule:

A name that starts with an underscore (_) is private to its library. Everything else is public.

A library is normally a single .dart file.

Public and private members

class BankAccount {
 String owner; // public
 double _balance = 0; // private to this file

 BankAccount(this.owner);

 double get balance => _balance;

 void deposit(double amount) {
 if (amount <= 0) throw ArgumentError('Deposit must be positive');
 _balance += amount;
 _log('deposit $amount');
 }

 void _log(String message) => print('[$owner] $message'); // private method
}

void main() {
 var account = BankAccount('Sarita');
 account.deposit(250);
 print(account.balance);
}

[Sarita] deposit 250.0
250.0

The underscore works on anything with a name: fields, methods, constructors, classes, top-level functions and variables.

item.title: Recursion in Dart: Functions That Call Themselves
item.description:
A recursive function is one that calls itself. It solves a problem by breaking it into a smaller version of the same problem, until the problem is small enough to answer directly.

The two parts of every recursive function

  1. Base case: the simple situation where the function returns an answer without calling itself.
  2. Recursive case: the function calls itself with a smaller input, moving towards the base case.

Leave out the base case and the function calls itself forever until the program crashes with a stack overflow.

item.title: Single-Subscription vs Broadcast Streams in Dart
item.description:
Dart has two kinds of stream. They share the same API but behave differently when it comes to who can listen and what happens to events nobody hears.

Single-subscription streams

This is the default. The stream allows one listener for its whole lifetime, and it does not start producing events until that listener arrives. Nothing is lost.

Stream<int> numbers() async* {
 print('(stream started)');
 yield 1;
 yield 2;
 yield 3;
}

Future<void> main() async {
 final stream = numbers();
 print('Created, not yet listening');

 await for (final n in stream) {
 print(n);
 }
}

Created, not yet listening
(stream started)
1
2
3

The body of numbers did not run until await for began listening.

item.title: Unit Testing in Dart with package:test
item.description:
A test is a small program that checks whether your code does what you expect. Tests catch mistakes before your users do, and they let you change code without fear, because one command tells you whether anything broke.

Set up

Projects made with dart create already include the test package. Otherwise:

dart pub add --dev test

Tests live in the test/ folder, in files whose names end with _test.dart.

The code under test

// File: lib/cart.dart

class Cart {
 final _items = <String, double>{};

 void add(String name, double price) {
 if (price < 0) throw ArgumentError('Price cannot be negative');
 _items[name] = price;
 }

 void remove(String name) => _items.remove(name);

 int get count => _items.length;
 bool get isEmpty => _items.isEmpty;
 double get total => _items.values.fold(0, (sum, p) => sum + p);

 double totalWithDiscount(double percent) => total * (1 - percent / 100);
}

A first test

// File: test/cart_test.dart
import 'package:my_app/cart.dart';
import 'package:test/test.dart';

void main() {
 test('a new cart is empty', () {
 final cart = Cart();

 expect(cart.isEmpty, isTrue);
 expect(cart.count, 0);
 expect(cart.total, 0);
 });

 test('total is the sum of item prices', () {
 final cart = Cart()
 ..add('pen', 20)
 ..add('book', 350);

 expect(cart.total, 370);
 });
}

test takes a description and a function. expect(actual, expected) passes when they match, and fails the test with a clear message when they do not.

item.title: Dart vs Python: Differences, Code Comparison and Which to Learn
item.description:
Python is the most popular first language for data science, automation and scripting. Dart is the language of Flutter, used to build apps for Android, iOS, web and desktop from one codebase. If you know Python, you already understand most of Dart’s ideas. This page shows the same code in both languages.

At a glance

Dart Python
Typing Static and sound, with type inference Dynamic (optional type hints)
Null Sound null safety: String? can be null, String cannot Any variable can be None
Blocks Curly braces { } and semicolons Indentation
Runs as Native code, JavaScript or WebAssembly Interpreted (CPython)
Speed Fast, compiled Slower for pure-Python loops
Main uses Flutter apps, CLI tools, servers Data science, AI, scripting, web back ends
Packages pub.dev (dart pub add) PyPI (pip install)

Hello world and variables

# Python
name = "Asha"
age = 21
print(f"{name} is {age}")

void main() {
 var name = 'Asha'; // type inferred: String
 int age = 21; // or write the type
 print('$name is $age');
}

Asha is 21

Dart code lives in functions; a program starts at main(). Every statement ends with ;. String interpolation uses $ instead of Python’s f-strings.

item.title: Math and Random Numbers in Dart: dart:math, Random, Rounding
item.description:
Dart’s basic number operators (+ - * / ~/ %) are always available. For square roots, powers, trigonometry, min / max and random numbers, import the dart:math library:

import 'dart:math';

Random numbers

import 'dart:math';

void main() {
 final random = Random();

 final dice = random.nextInt(6) + 1; // 1 to 6
 final chance = random.nextDouble(); // 0.0 up to (not including) 1.0
 final coin = random.nextBool(); // true or false

 print('dice: $dice');
 print('chance below 1: ${chance < 1}');
 print('coin: ${coin ? 'heads' : 'tails'}');
}

dice: 4
chance below 1: true
coin: heads

Your numbers will be different each time you press Run.

item.title: What's New in Dart 3: Modern Features from 3.0 to 3.10
item.description:
Dart improves every few months. If you learned Dart from an older tutorial, this page shows the modern features you may have missed, newest last, each with a small example you can run. Every lesson on this site already uses modern Dart.

To use a feature, your installed Dart must be new enough and your pubspec.yaml must allow it:

environment:
 sdk: ^3.10.0  # the lower bound turns language features on

Check your version with dart --version, and upgrade as shown in install Dart.

item.title: Handling File Errors in Dart
item.description:
File operations depend on things outside your program: the disk, permissions, other programs. Any of them can fail. Good file code expects that.

FileSystemException

Nearly every failure in dart:io is reported as a FileSystemException, or one of its subclasses.

import 'dart:io';

Future<void> main() async {
 try {
 await File('/no/such/folder/data.txt').readAsString();
 } on FileSystemException catch (e) {
 print('Message: ${e.message}');
 print('Path: ${e.path}');
 print('OS error: ${e.osError?.message} (code ${e.osError?.errorCode})');
 }
}

Message: Cannot open file
Path: /no/such/folder/data.txt
OS error: No such file or directory (code 2)
Property Contains
message What Dart was trying to do
path The file or directory involved
osError The operating system’s own explanation and error code

Specific subclasses

Catch the specific type when you want to react to one cause in particular.

item.title: Iterable in Dart: Lazy Sequences Explained
item.description:
An Iterable is anything you can step through one item at a time. List and Set are both iterables, and so are the results of methods like where and map. Understanding iterables explains two things beginners find puzzling: why results print with round brackets, and why .toList() shows up everywhere.

Results are iterables, not lists

void main() {
 var numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6];

 var evens = numbers.where((n) => n.isEven);
 print(evens);
 print(evens.toList());
}

(2, 4, 6)
[2, 4, 6]

The round brackets tell you evens is a plain iterable. It supports for-in, length, first, contains and so on, but not [index], add or sort. Call toList() or toSet() when you need those.

item.title: Operators in Dart: Arithmetic, Comparison, Logical and More
item.description:
An operator is a symbol that works on one or more values. You have already used + and ==. This lesson collects all the common ones in one place.

Arithmetic

Operator Meaning 7 ? 2
+ Add 9
- Subtract 5
* Multiply 14
/ Divide 3.5
~/ Integer divide 3
% Remainder 1

Assignment

void main() {
 var x = 10;
 x += 5; // x = x + 5
 print(x);
 x -= 3;
 print(x);
 x *= 2;
 print(x);
 x ~/= 5;
 print(x);
}

15
12
24
4

Increment and decrement

++ adds one and -- subtracts one. Placed before the name, the change happens first. Placed after, the old value is used first.

item.title: Running Futures in Parallel in Dart: Future.wait and More
item.description:
When several asynchronous tasks do not depend on each other, start them all and wait for them together. The total time is then that of the slowest task, not the sum of all of them.

The slow way

Future<String> fetch(String name, int ms) =>
 Future.delayed(Duration(milliseconds: ms), () => name);

Future<void> main() async {
 final watch = Stopwatch()..start();

 final user = await fetch('user', 600);
 final posts = await fetch('posts', 600);
 final friends = await fetch('friends', 600);

 print('$user, $posts, $friends');
 print('Took about ${(watch.elapsedMilliseconds / 100).round() / 10}s');
}

user, posts, friends
Took about 1.8s

Each await waits for the one before, although none of them needs the others.

item.title: Static Variables and Methods in Dart
item.description:
Normal fields and methods belong to each object. A static member belongs to the class itself. There is one copy, shared by everyone, and you use it through the class name.

Static variables

class Visitor {
 static int count = 0; // one shared counter
 final String name; // one per object

 Visitor(this.name) {
 count++;
 }
}

void main() {
 Visitor('Anil');
 Visitor('Bina');
 Visitor('Chitra');

 print(Visitor.count);
}

3

Every Visitor has its own name, but there is only one count.

Static constants

The most common static member is a constant that belongs with a class.

item.title: typedef in Dart: Naming Function and Other Types
item.description:
A typedef gives a type a second name. It does not create a new type. It is a shortcut that makes long types readable and keeps them in one place.

The problem it solves

Function types get long quickly.

void fetchUser(
 int id,
 void Function(String name, int age) onSuccess,
 void Function(String message) onError,
) {
 if (id > 0) {
 onSuccess('Kiran', 28);
 } else {
 onError('Invalid id');
 }
}

void main() {
 fetchUser(1, (name, age) => print('$name, $age'), print);
}

Naming the function types

typedef UserCallback = void Function(String name, int age);
typedef ErrorCallback = void Function(String message);

void fetchUser(int id, UserCallback onSuccess, ErrorCallback onError) {
 if (id > 0) {
 onSuccess('Kiran', 28);
 } else {
 onError('Invalid id');
 }
}

void main() {
 fetchUser(1, (name, age) => print('$name, $age'), print);
 fetchUser(-1, (name, age) => print('$name, $age'), print);
}

Kiran, 28
Invalid id

The signature of fetchUser now fits on one line and says what each callback is for.

item.title: Build a REST API in Dart with Shelf: Routes, JSON and Middleware
item.description:
Dart is not only for apps. With the official shelf package you can write an HTTP server, and the same language then powers both your Flutter app and its back end. In this lesson you build a small to-do REST API.

You need Dart installed on your computer for this lesson, because a server cannot run in the browser. See install Dart.

1. Create the project

dart create -t server-shelf todo_api
cd todo_api
dart run bin/server.dart

The server-shelf template already includes shelf and shelf_router. Open http://localhost:8080/ in your browser and you will see Hello, World!.

item.title: Completer in Dart: Creating Futures You Complete Yourself
item.description:
Normally an async function creates and completes its future for you. A Completer lets you create a future and complete it yourself, later, from anywhere. It is a low-level tool for the few cases async/await cannot express.

The basics

A completer has two sides:

  • completer.future is what you give to the code that waits.
  • completer.complete(value) or completer.completeError(error) is what you call when the result is known.
import 'dart:async';

Future<void> main() async {
 final completer = Completer<String>();

 // Somewhere else, later:
 Timer(Duration(seconds: 1), () {
 completer.complete('The result');
 });

 print('Waiting...');
 final value = await completer.future;
 print(value);
}

Waiting...
The result

Main use: wrapping a callback-style API

Some older libraries and platform APIs report results by calling a function you pass in. A completer turns that into a future you can await.

item.title: final vs const in Dart: Values That Do Not Change
item.description:
